newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Chance crude stock draw seen in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Chance crude stock draw seen in APIs.

text.p: Tuesday's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected by some traders to show a rise in crude stocks due to imports, but there is just as strong a chance for a draw, others said.

A consensus of trader estimates forecasted a rise of one million barrels in the data that reflects the week ended April 18. But, estimates ranged from up 3.5 million barrels to down two million barrels.
"Last week's import numbers were just too low, so we should get a correction to that this week," said Jim Ritterbush, trader with Sweeney Oil in Illinois.
For the week ended April 11, the API said imports fell 340,000 barrels per day (bpd) to well below eight million, a level which Ritterbush expects will be reached in this week's data.
"Runs have been strong enough to absorb a lot of crude, and we are due for an adjustment to all the builds we have gotten recently," said John Saucer, an analyst with Smith Barney in Houston said.
"We are due for a temporary respite from the lofty import levels we have seen," said William Brown, president of trading firm W.H. Brown & Co in New York.

Imports in PADDS one to four eased to 7.56 million barrels per day (bpd), excluding those from Canada, in last week's data after rising to 7.90 million bpd the week before. Moreover, crude runs were seen steady with last week's high 14.2 million bpd.

Implied demand for gasoline was seen picking up after dropping to a seasonally low 7.3 million bpd to a more realistic level of 7.7 to 7.8 million bpd. The demand increase should trigger a decline in gasoline stocks of one to 2.5 million barrels, dealer said.

Distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, were seen off by about half million barrels. Distillate demand was expected to have increased from a low 3.1 million bpd amid unseasonably cold weather in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States.
